key_insight: ASCENT exposes a gap between answering fully specified medical questions and updating diagnostic reasoning as clinical information arrives.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark supports evaluation of reasoning in workflows resembling staged clinical assessment, without establishing readiness for patient care.
method: Constructed 3,078 clinician-annotated stepwise problems from MedQA-USMLE.
Organized vignettes into EMR-aligned Findings, Impression, and supporting Rationale steps.
Evaluated LLMs, fine-tuned Qwen2.5 models, and tested robustness to altered prior impressions and sequential rollout.
evidence_signal: ASCENT fine-tuning improved F1 for Qwen2.5-7B and 32B over pre-trained and HuatuoGPT-o1 CoT-trained baselines, primarily through precision gains.
watch_item: Errors can propagate across sequential diagnostic steps, and exam-derived benchmark gains do not establish real-world clinical safety.
paper_title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
